# Page 3^page=3
Turbine Startup and Run C hecklist ___: Refer to Quick Reference. 1. MCR - Condenser Vacuum within acceptable limits. 2. MCR - Reactor Online at 20% Average Power Range. 3. MCR - Main Steam Line Pressure around 7 MPa, 7100 kPa optimal. 4. MCR - Electrical Distribution Panel Configured. 5. MCR - RPV Water Level Optimal. 6. TH - If actuated, Reset Stop Valves Actuator. 7. TH - Open Lubrication Oil Valves in Turbine Hall. 8. TH - Replace Oil Filters as required. 9. TH - Generator Cool Air Valve Open 100%. 10. AUX Hydraulic Pump ON, ensure running. 11. AUX Lubrication Pump ON, ensure running. 12. Enable Oil Cooling and Steam Sealing AUTO. 13. Engage Turning Gear and Preheat Turbine Casing to 270°C. 14. At sufficient Casing Temperature, disable the turning gear. 15. When the turbine RPM hits 0, disengage the turning gear. 16. Confirm that the turbine is ready for runup and call MCR. 17. Once above 1800 RPM, turn the Hydraulic and Lubrication Pumps OFF. 18. During High Humidity Operations, open the warm air valve to 45%. 19. Watch the generator temperature. If too high, request MCR to reduce the load. 20. After High Humidity Operations Concluded, Close Warm Air Valve to 0%

# Page 4^page=4
Quick Reference 4. Ensure that there is power to B US A and B US S before attempting startup, as well as enabling rolldown protection if disabled; otherwise, the turbine cannot be run up. 5. Optimal RPV water level 0m. High water level (3m) will inhibit turbine runup, and low water level may trip the reactor (at -3m). C ontrolling the cooling circuit levels is elaborated on in the U2 MC R guide. 6. Go to the back of the Unit 2 turbine and check if the valves are actuated. You will see a red cylinder; click on it to push it back down, which will reset the stop valve actuator. The turbine cannot be run up if the valves are actuated. 8. A ny dirty oil filters need to be replaced to prevent potential turbine trips. D isassemble the filter container, take out the dirty filter, and dispose of it in the special waste storage facility. Then, get a new filter and replace it. A fterwards, close the container again. 9. The air valves are located below the Unit 2 Turbine Generator in the C ondenser Hall. C limb up the ladder, go between the electrical equipment to the next ladder, and climb up to the warm and cold air valves for the generator.

# Page 5^page=5
13. Enable the turning gear after it has been engaged and open the preheat valve to 100%. A fter the casing temperature reaches 270°C , close the preheat valve fully. 16. C heck the turbine parameters; if they are all in the green, then the turbine still may not be started, as there could be an underlying issue, i.e., rolldown protection disabled, RPV water level high, and/or the stop valves actuator is engaged. If there is no underlying issue, then call the MC R stating “Turbine ready for run-up”. Note that due to roblox chat restrictions the PMS (plant messaging system) would be a more effective means of communicating that the turbine is ready for run-up. 19. If there is no high humidity and the warm air valve is open, fully close the valve, and ensure the cold air valve is open 100%. If this still doesn’t fix it, then request a load decrease. If there is high humidity and the temperature is high, request a load decrease immediately.

# Page 6^page=6
Emergency Procedures This section will give you a summary and understanding of how turbine events occur and what to do to mitigate their effects or correct/repair them. The following events can occur even if “Random Malfunctions” are off: steam leaks, turbine damage, oil spray, turbine smoke, and turbine fires. They are commonly caused by operator negligence. For the turbine smoke or spray events, handheld guides can be found in the turbine control room. Steam Leak Low steam sealing pressure will cause radioactive steam to leak from the turbine, and an audible hissing noise can be heard. The more severe the leak, the more visible the steam will be and the louder the hissing, not to mention higher doses of radiation if close to the leak. Sealing pressure should immediately be restored to normal parameters and reported to the MC R. A sealing pressure of 0 will cause a turbine trip. Steam leaks can also be identified by the “HIGH RA D IATION SENSOR 8” annunciator, which will deactivate after a period of time since the steam sealing pressure is restored, or after a short period since the turbine shutdown. A low-steam-flow (low power) steam leak: A high steam flow (high power) steam leak:

# Page 7^page=7
Hydraulic Oil Leak This is a randomly occurring event that only occurs when Random Malfunctions are enabled. It can be identified by the hydraulic oil pressure decreasing at a nearly constant rate. The turbine should be shut down. If operations are continued, closing the backflow valve will raise the oil pressure temporarily, and then it will continue to drop at the same rate. Ultimately, the turbine will need to be shut down anyway, and the leak should be repaired by the turbine maintenance crew. Turbine D amage Will occur under the following conditions: high turbine vibrations (>=6), High (or low) oil temperature, high (or low) oil pressure. Turbine damage cannot occur at <= 50 RPM. Slight turbine damage itself is not immediately a cause for alarm; however, it may eventually lead to a turbine oil spray or a turbine smoke event, both of which will mandate immediate turbine shutdown. Turbine vibrations >0 (while synced to the grid) is an indicator of damage. Turbine Oil Spray Random chance of occurring after turbine health reaches 0. Oil can be seen spraying from the low-pressure and high-pressure turbine connecting pipes. Trip the turbine, disable hydraulic and lubrication pumps, and close all of the oil valves in the turbine hall, starting from the valves furthest from the exit. The handheld guide will have more details. If the turbine catches fire, refer to the turbine fire subsection. Turbine Smoke Random chance of occurring after turbine health reaches below 60%. B lue smoke can be seen originating from the low-pressure and high-pressure turbine connection pipes. Trip the turbine and disable the hydraulic and lubrication oil pumps. Once the turbine RPM reaches 0, you can request that the turbine maintenance crew repair the turbine. The handheld guide will go into more detail.

# Page 8^page=8
Turbine Fire C an occur if the turbine oil spray is left unchecked. The chances of a fire igniting are reduced if all necessary precautions are taken. D uring this event, roaring flames can be seen and heard. The turbine must be tripped immediately, and halon is to be discharged by pulling one of the call points to extinguish the fire (if not done already). When halon is discharged, immediately evacuate the turbine hall to avoid suffocation. A photo of a turbine fire in progress A photo of a halon discharge in progress

# Page 9^page=9
Manual C ontrol Steam Sealing Optimal sealing pressure is 0.25 bar. If the sealing pressure is too high, then you need to move the switch to the leak-off position; if the pressure is too low, then you need to move it to the supply position. When preparing for turbine runup initially, the supply valve may need to be fully opened to gain optimal sealing pressure. However, it should be immediately reduced when steam enters the turbine during run-up. A s generator load increases, sealing pressure will increase, and vice versa. Oil Temperature The lubrication oil temperature should remain at around 44°C . A t lower generator loads or during turbine run-up, the warm water valve may need to be used alongside the cold water valve to maintain this temperature. D uring high generator loads, above ~70 A PRM, the warm water valve should be fully closed (unless still needed), and the cool water valve should be used primarily for maintaining the desired temperatures. Oil Pressure The backflow valve is the primary method of maintaining oil pressure. While other methods are possible, such as reducing the oil pump valve, the backflow valve should be primarily used during operations. Oil pressure should be around 12 bar at all times because incorrect oil pressure (too high/too low) will cause turbine damage. C lose the backflow valve to increase oil pressure, and open it to decrease pressure. If the oil pressure is still low even if the backflow valve is at 70%, refer to the Hydraulic Oil Leak subsection. The backflow valve should be at 100% all the time unless the oil pressure is too low. Any Questions? If content is missing, obscure, or incorrect, message any writer of this document. You may also join training sessions.
